notes.mpola: Also a way of life: no rush.
notes.siteegi: Kituo cha basi: bus stop. Kituoni: at the station.
notes.uwanja-wa-ndege: Literally “field of birds”: ndege is both bird and plane.
notes.mmotoka: Plural: magari. It takes ji- agreement: gari langu jipya.

guidebook.intro: Buses, trains and planes connect the towns of East Africa. Here you’ll plan a journey and learn to talk about the future.

tips.title: The future: -ta-
body: Put **-ta-** where **-na-** was and you are talking about the future: **ninasafiri** (I’m travelling) becomes **nitasafiri** (I will travel). Notice **nina-** shortens to **ni-**.
It works for everyone: **utasafiri** (you will), **tutaondoka** (we will leave), **treni itafika** (the train will arrive). Ask when with **lini** at the end: **Utasafiri lini?**

tips.title: Gari and its friends
body: Some nouns have no prefix in the singular and **ma-** in the plural: **gari, magari**; **jibu, majibu**; **swali, maswali**. Their describing words take **ji-** or **l-**: **gari langu jipya** (my new car), **swali la tatu** (the third question).
In the plural they all use **ma-** forms: **magari mapya**, **maswali yangu**.

culture.title: Pole pole, but on time
body: Long-distance buses leave when they are full, and a **matatu** may wait a while. Trains and planes do not: for those, **mapema** (early) is the rule.
